_about.what: Which coarse area of the car a fault code points at. A DTC (the 5-character code an engine computer stores, e.g. 'P0217') encodes its system in its prefix, so zone is derived from the prefix rather than stored per code.
_about.why_it_matters: Zone is not just a label on the dashboard — it routes the parts catalog (MKT-1) and the planned 3D 'highlight the affected area' view. A wrong zone recommends the wrong parts to a driver.
_about.why_a_file: These mappings are editorial judgements that will be revised against the OBD-II ranges. As data, a revision is a reviewable diff against a source; as code, it is an edit to a file that also holds the lookup logic. The rules (which table to consult, in what order, and the fallbacks) stay in faults.py — only the mappings live here.
_about.notes_are_not_asserted: Every entry carries a 'note' explaining the range it covers. These are for the human revising the table and are never read by the code.
_about.unverified: The p04_third_digit assignments and the coarseness of powertrain_family are the parts most in need of checking against a real source. In particular every P-code family that is not listed here collapses to 'engine', which lumps fuel/air metering (P01xx, P02xx), auxiliary inputs (P05xx) and computer output (P06xx) into one bucket.

C.note: Cxxxx — brakes, steering, suspension, wheel speed

03.note: P03xx — misfires and the ignition system

empty_code.note: Nothing to classify — must not raise.

p04.note: A P04xx code we cannot narrow (e.g. truncated 'P04'). 'Emissions' is the range's own name, so it is the honest answer.

powertrain.note: Any P-code family without its own entry above. Deliberately coarse — see _about.unverified.
